ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Marie Curie Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for two months of fatigue, breathlessness on stairs, easy bruising, and a recent fever. Concerns: Exhausted and short of breath for two months, with bruises she cannot explain; Wonders whether her years of radiation work caused this, and wants her laboratory staff protected; Blurred, glary vision in the right eye is slowing her reading. [S]

Two tablets by mouth once daily, two hours before or four hours after food, dairy, or antacids
Acyclovir 400 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice daily during immunosuppression
One tablet by mouth twice daily

tr.td: Primary care visit for two months of fatigue, breathlessness on stairs, easy bruising, and a recent fever
Hematology consultation with bone marrow aspirate and biopsy for pancytopenia
Primary care follow-up three weeks after starting immunosuppressive therapy, with a cataract and eye review
Primary care follow-up six weeks into immunosuppressive therapy, after laser capsulotomy of the right eye
Urgent hematology referral for pancytopenia with a low reticulocyte count, for bone marrow aspirate and biopsy, cytogenetics, and PNH testing
Initial anemia workup in primary care: CBC with differential and reticulocyte count, blood film, vitamin B12, folate, ferritin, LDH, bilirubin, and kidney function

Supportive care: irradiated, leukocyte-depleted red cells for symptomatic anemia; platelet thresholds set by hematology; same-day assessment for a temperature of 38 °C or higher; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs
Record cumulative occupational radiation exposure, stop further exposure while counts recover, and review shielding and dosimetry for laboratory staff with occupational health
First-line immunosuppressive therapy given by hematology: horse antithymocyte globulin with cyclosporine and eltrombopag, plus acyclovir prophylaxis; inactivated vaccines only
Monitor CBC weekly during the first months of treatment, with kidney function, potassium, and ALT every two weeks on cyclosporine and eltrombopag

Comprehensive dilated eye examination with best-corrected acuity, intraocular pressure, slit-lamp examination, and a functional vision assessment; YAG laser capsulotomy when capsule opacification limits daily tasks; eye examinations every one to two years afterward
Hematology evaluation with bone marrow biopsy within one week of the pancytopenia result
Seen and biopsied seven days after the first visit
No serious infection or bleeding during the first months of treatment
No infection or bleeding through the sixth week of therapy
Early rise in neutrophil and platelet counts by the six-week visit
Neutrophils rose from 0.4 to 0.8 and platelets from 18 to 34 thousand per microliter; formal response is judged at three to six months
Read standard print comfortably with the right eye after capsulotomy
Reading without glare one week after laser capsulotomy
